privacy.metaDescription: How Menuyukti collects, uses, and protects data in your workspace.
privacy.title: Privacy Policy

data.title: Data we process
data.body: Menuyukti processes information you provide when you use the product—including account details, location and sales data you upload, workflow and milestone content, and usage needed to run the service. We process this data to deliver analytics, workflows, and AI-assisted features you request.

use.title: How we use your data
use.body: We use your data to operate and improve the platform, provide support, secure accounts, and comply with law. We do not sell your personal information or your restaurant sales data to third parties for their marketing.

sharing.title: Service providers
sharing.body: We may use trusted subprocessors (for example hosting, authentication, and AI inference) that process data under contract and only as needed to provide the service. A current list can be provided on request.

security.title: Security
security.body: We apply reasonable technical and organizational measures designed to protect your information. No method of transmission or storage is completely secure; we encourage strong passwords and safe sharing of workspace access.

cookies.title: Cookies and analytics
cookies.body: Menuyukti loads Google Analytics 4 only on our print shop pages (/shop), and only after you accept analytics in the cookie banner. If you choose Essentials only, no analytics scripts are loaded and no analytics cookies are set. You can change your choice anytime via the Cookie settings link in the footer.

contact.title: Contact
contact.body: For privacy-related questions or requests, contact us through the same channel you use for Menuyukti product support.

terms.metaDescription: Terms governing use of the Menuyukti platform.
terms.title: Terms of Service

service.title: The service
service.body: Menuyukti provides software for restaurant marketing workflows, analytics, and related AI-assisted features. Features may change as the product evolves.

account.title: Your account
account.body: You are responsible for activity under your account and for keeping credentials secure. You agree to provide accurate information and to use the service in compliance with applicable law.

acceptable.title: Acceptable use
acceptable.body: You may not misuse the service, attempt to access others’ data without permission, interfere with operation of the platform, or use the service to violate law or third-party rights.

disclaimer.title: Disclaimer
disclaimer.body: The service and any AI-generated outputs are provided on an “as is” basis. Analytics and suggestions are informational; you remain responsible for business and compliance decisions.

changes.title: Changes
changes.body: We may update these terms or the service. Continued use after changes constitutes acceptance of the updated terms where permitted by law.

faq.title: Common questions
faq.q1: What data do I need to upload?
faq.a1: For Pro workflows and sales-grounded AI analytics, upload your POS sales report (where your POS format is supported) so we can normalize columns and build demand, mix, and timing signals. Studio AI generation and strategy chat do not require sales data to be useful; the print shop never requires uploads.
faq.q2: Do I need sales data to use Studio or the print shop?
faq.a2: No. Studio and strategy chat do not require sales uploads. Connecting reports unlocks smarter, evidence-backed Pro automation. The print shop is standalone artwork you can browse anytime as an add-on.
faq.q3: What is an agentic AI system?
faq.a3: An agentic AI system goes beyond a single chat reply: it can plan steps, call tools, and run multi-milestone workflows toward a goal—like a teammate following a brief. In Menuyukti, that shows up strongest in Pro campaign pipelines that turn sales signals into schedules, promotion ideas, and copy. You stay in control with inspectable runs and workspace data, while the system handles repetitive orchestration.
faq.a4: Restaurant owners, operators, and solo marketers who run social media for small to mid-sized restaurants and want faster Instagram execution with stronger data-backed decisions.
faq.a5: Yes. You can share workflows, milestones, and brand assets when you bring in collaborators.

post_scheduler.label: Scheduler
post_scheduler.title: Scheduler
post_scheduler.inputDescription: Optional guidance for cadence, content-format mix (Reels/feed), dayparts, or weekend/holiday preferences. The run uses Campaign Brief context plus prefetched promotion candidates (star/puzzle menu items).
post_scheduler.inputPlaceholder: e.g. 3 content slots per week; avoid weekends; prefer Reels for hero dishes…
post_scheduler.goal: Generate a schedule of Instagram content for the campaign window: each entry has weekday, date, time, format details (Reel/Post and Carousel/Single), promoted menu items grounded in prefetched promotion candidates, and a caption idea aligned with the campaign brief.
post_scheduler.criterionPostsGenerated: **Posts** in the data is a non-empty array when the campaign dates and promotion context support a schedule; otherwise document why the list is empty.
post_scheduler.criterionPostFields: Each post includes **dayOfWeek**, **date** (YYYY-MM-DD), **time**, **postType** (`Reel` or `Post`), **contentType** (`Carousel` or `Single`), **promotedMenuItems**, and **captionIdea**. For multi-post schedules, include a format mix: at least one `Reel` and one `Post`, plus at least one `Carousel` and one `Single`.
post_scheduler.criterionMenuItems: **Promoted menu items** only name dishes that appear in prefetched promotion candidates (star/puzzle items), not invented items.

promotion_candidates.label: Promotion candidates
promotion_candidates.title: Promotion candidates
promotion_candidates.inputDescription: Optional orientation notes for how to review star/puzzle candidates in this campaign context.
promotion_candidates.inputPlaceholder: e.g. prioritize FOOD first this month due to family bundles...
promotion_candidates.goal: Fetch promotion-engineering candidates and present star and puzzle menu items by category. Use Campaign Brief main category to place the most relevant category first in preview.
promotion_candidates.criterionCategoriesPresent: Data includes at least one category section (**FOOD** or **DRINK**), and the first category matches `mainCategory` in the same data payload.
promotion_candidates.criterionItemsOnlyFromSignals: **starItems** and **puzzleItems** only include menu names from promotion-engineering signals (no invented items).

culture_hooks.label: Culture hooks
culture_hooks.title: Culture hooks
culture_hooks.inputDescription: Optional direction for tone and emphasis. The run uses only prior Campaign Brief data to infer location concept, target audience, and non-food intersection topics.
culture_hooks.inputPlaceholder: e.g. prioritize sustainability and family rituals with retro tone...
culture_hooks.goal: Use Campaign Brief data to identify the location concept and target audience, then generate intersection topics between the concept and the audience's likely interests (not necessarily food). These intersections should be actionable for Instagram Reels ideas that attract potential new customers.
culture_hooks.criterionIntersectionsPresent: Data includes **3-5 non-food intersections** with concrete topic, concept link, audience relevance, and content example.
culture_hooks.criterionNonFood: Intersections are **not food-centric** (no dish names, recipes, or flavor-led angles).
culture_hooks.criterionAudienceConceptInferred: Data clearly states **locationConcept** and **targetAudience**, both inferred from Campaign Brief context.

format_mix.label: Format mix
format_mix.title: Format mix
format_mix.inputDescription: Optional guidance for how you want to weight Instagram formats (single posts, carousels, Reels). The run reads your prior Campaign Brief for context.
format_mix.inputPlaceholder: e.g. lean on Reels for launches; keep carousels for menus…
format_mix.goal: Define a target share of Instagram formats (single posts, carousels, single-video Reels, multi-video Reels) for the campaign, grounded in the Campaign Brief. The run loads prior brief data first; percentage targets are filled when you generate or edit structured data.
format_mix.criterionBriefGrounded: Work is **consistent with prior Campaign Brief** context (objective, audience, pillars)—no contradictions unless assumptions are stated.
format_mix.criterionMixDefined: Data includes a **formats** array with at least one entry, each with **format** and **percent** (0–100), when the campaign warrants a mix; otherwise document why the list is empty.

restaurant_campaign_brief.label: Campaign brief
restaurant_campaign_brief.title: Campaign brief
restaurant_campaign_brief.inputDescription: Optional context for generation (style, positioning, constraints). Example: during a soccer World Cup period, note campaign priorities or tone for match days. Included with location and analytics data when you run or generate the brief.
restaurant_campaign_brief.inputPlaceholder: e.g. Family-friendly trattoria tone; highlight lunch and vegetarian options…
restaurant_campaign_brief.goal: The data holds a factual campaign brief foundation: campaign window (`startDate`, `endDate`) with public holidays, venue snapshot, objective and funnel stage, target segments, message hierarchy, CTA/offer plan, content and proof strategy, plus measurement/testing/risk guardrails grounded in available analytics.
restaurant_campaign_brief.criterionStartDate: **startDate** is set in the data using the Input tab campaign window.
restaurant_campaign_brief.criterionEndDate: **endDate** is set in the data using the Input tab campaign window.
restaurant_campaign_brief.criterionPublicHolidays: **publicHolidays** is generated for the campaign window and listed in the data.
restaurant_campaign_brief.criterionVenueSnapshot: **Venue snapshot** in the data names the venue and uses city/country/currency when known; it does not invent full addresses.
restaurant_campaign_brief.criterionContentPillars: **Content pillars** include 3-5 unique non-empty items that are concrete enough to guide campaign content.
restaurant_campaign_brief.criterionAudienceHypotheses: **Audience hypotheses** include 3-5 unique non-empty items that are plausible for the venue context and usable for campaign planning. They should align with available data signals when present, but exact signal keywords or strict demographic proof in every line are optional. Fail only when items are empty, duplicated, or clearly disconnected from context.
restaurant_campaign_brief.criterionProofAngles: **Proof-oriented angles** include 3-5 unique non-empty items and are concrete, evidence-oriented reasons to believe the campaign message. They should align with known venue/menu context when available; naming exact menu items or category labels in every line is optional.
restaurant_campaign_brief.criterionToneGuardrails: **Tone guardrails** include 3-5 unique non-empty items that are coherent with venue context and provide usable writing constraints.
restaurant_campaign_brief.criterionCampaignObjective: **Campaign objective** states one primary business outcome and a dominant funnel stage. Equivalent stage phrasing is acceptable.
restaurant_campaign_brief.criterionTargetSegments: **Target segments** include 3-5 unique non-empty items that are actionable for campaign planning. Pass when segments are clear and usable; strict taxonomy is optional.
restaurant_campaign_brief.criterionMessageHierarchy: **Message hierarchy** includes 3-5 unique lines with a clear priority order for promise, proof, and call-to-action across the set. Exact wording in each line is flexible.
restaurant_campaign_brief.criterionOfferAndCtaPlan: **Offer and CTA plan** includes 3-5 unique lines that explain realistic guest actions and margin-safe offer framing. Not every line needs every channel.
restaurant_campaign_brief.criterionContentPillarPlan: **Content pillar plan** includes 3-5 unique lines mapping pillars to executable campaign guidance (such as angle, format, or CTA emphasis). Rigid templates are optional.
restaurant_campaign_brief.criterionMeasurementPlan: **Measurement plan** includes 3-5 unique lines with clear metrics and practical decision signals. Exact threshold phrasing is optional if decision intent is clear.
restaurant_campaign_brief.criterionTestingPlan: **Testing plan** includes 3-5 unique lines with concrete experiments and follow-up actions when performance is weak. Exact test taxonomy is optional.
restaurant_campaign_brief.criterionRiskGuardrails: **Risk guardrails** include 3-5 unique lines covering brand, regulatory, or operational constraints and clear avoidances where relevant.

chat.milestoneCampaignBriefPreviewHelpVenueSn: The venue snapshot names where you operate (city, country, currency) so Instagram geotags, local collaborations, and “visit us” language stay accurate—not invented addresses.
chat.milestoneCampaignBriefPreviewHelpContent: Content pillars are recurring themes for your feed (for example brunch, chef favorites, or weekday lunch). They keep Stories and Reels coherent so you rotate angles without random one-off topics.
chat.milestoneCampaignBriefPreviewHelpAudienc: Audience hypotheses describe who you expect to reach and when, grounded in your data. They guide posting times, tone, and creative hooks so Instagram content matches real behavior, not generic demographics alone.
chat.milestoneCampaignBriefPreviewHelpProofOr: Proof-oriented angles are evidence-backed reasons to believe you (dishes, operations, social proof). They make captions and Reels credible and specific—stronger than generic “best in town” claims.
chat.milestoneCampaignBriefPreviewHelpToneGua: Tone guardrails define voice and boundaries for Instagram copy, replies, and community management so messaging stays on-brand and avoids mismatched humor or claims.
chat.milestoneCampaignBriefPreviewHelpCampaig: The campaign objective states what success looks like (for example awareness vs bookings). It aligns CTAs, offers, and what you optimize for in Instagram analytics.
chat.milestoneCampaignBriefPreviewHelpTargetS: Target segments are moment-based clusters (for example weekday lunch vs weekend families). They let you tailor hooks and formats to when those audiences actually scroll.
chat.milestoneCampaignBriefPreviewHelpMessage: Message hierarchy orders your lead promise, proof, and call-to-action. It keeps single-image posts and short Reels legible so viewers know what to do after three seconds.
chat.milestoneCampaignBriefPreviewHelpOfferAn: The offer and CTA plan ties asks (reserve, DM, order, walk-in) to constraints that protect margin. It prevents Instagram promos from promising what ops cannot honor.
chat.milestoneCampaignBriefPreviewHelpContent: The content pillar plan maps each pillar to objective, format bias, and CTA role so scheduling balances Reels, carousels, and Stories across the campaign—not only one content type.
chat.milestoneCampaignBriefPreviewHelpMeasure: The measurement plan lists what to watch weekly or monthly on Instagram (and related signals) so you know whether the brief is working before the campaign ends.
chat.milestoneCampaignBriefPreviewHelpTesting: The testing plan defines what to try by daypart, day of week, or format—and what to change if results lag—so learning is explicit, not accidental A/B on the fly.
chat.milestoneCampaignBriefPreviewHelpRiskGua: Risk guardrails cover brand, regulatory, and operational limits plus topics or visuals to avoid—critical for alcohol, health claims, minors, and licensed imagery on a public channel.
chat.milestoneCampaignBriefPreviewHelpStartDa: Start date anchors when campaign messaging and scheduling begin—used for countdown posts, holiday overlap, and aligning promotion candidates and the scheduler.
chat.milestoneCampaignBriefPreviewHelpEndDate: End date marks when offers or campaign-specific messaging should stop so Instagram posts do not advertise expired deals or past windows.
chat.milestoneCampaignBriefPreviewHelpPublicH: Public holidays in the campaign window help you plan timely posts (hours, specials, cultural moments) and avoid surprises when the kitchen or traffic pattern shifts.
chat.milestonePostSchedulerPreviewEmptyWeekly: No weekly slot plan generated yet.
chat.milestonePostSchedulerPreviewHelpMonthly: The monthly arc splits the campaign into weekly beats so objectives evolve instead of repeating the same message. Use it to align Stories and Reels with what you are pushing that week.
chat.milestonePostSchedulerPreviewHelpContent: Content ratio shows how much of the feed each pillar should earn (for example chef stories vs promos). It keeps the mix balanced so you do not accidentally post only discounts or only behind-the-scenes.
chat.milestonePostSchedulerPreviewHelpFormatM: Format mix counts how many Reels, carousels, Stories, or static posts to plan. It matches creative workload to what your team can produce while still varying the feed.
chat.milestonePostSchedulerPreviewHelpWeeklyS: Each slot is one planned post: day, format, hook, caption shape, CTA, funnel stage, and visual direction. Hand this to whoever shoots or writes captions so every post has a clear job.
chat.milestonePostSchedulerPreviewHelpGuardra: Guardrail check is a quick sanity pass—timing, tone, offers, and operational limits—so scheduled ideas stay realistic for your kitchen, hours, and brand rules.
chat.milestonePromotionCandidatesPreviewSumma: Star items sell well; puzzle items sell less but may have margin or story upside. Use this list to decide what to feature, discount, or reframe on Instagram.
chat.milestonePromotionCandidatesPreviewHelpH: Promotion candidates come from menu engineering on your sales data. They are grouped by menu category so you can brief the kitchen and marketing on the same shortlist.
chat.milestonePromotionCandidatesPreviewHelpS: Star items are high performers on the menu. They are safe anchors for promos and hero posts because guests already choose them often.
chat.milestonePromotionCandidatesPreviewHelpP: Puzzle items are not top sellers yet. They may deserve better photos, bundling, or storytelling—or a gentle nudge off the menu if they tie up the line.
chat.milestonePromotionCandidatesPreviewHelpS: Storytelling fit estimates how easy it is to make an authentic Instagram story around a dish—local ingredients, craft, ritual, or culture—not just food styling.
